input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Bug report

Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

### Expected behavior
Sessions remain valid for the configured session lifetime.

### Actual behavior
Users are logged out after about 5 minutes.

### Suggested investigation
- Check session/token expiry and TTL settings in the login flow (e.g. access token lifetime, session cookie max-age).
- Check whether refresh tokens are issued and used correctly.
- Check for any hard-coded 5-minute timeout or cache/expiry values.

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out after approximately 5 minutes of activity.

## Likely area
The login code lives in the `acme-labs/auth-service` GitHub repository. Session/token expiry and refresh handling there is a likely cause.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the app.
2. Wait about 5 minutes (while using the app).
3. Observe that the session ends and the user is logged out.

## Expected behavior
The user remains logged in for the normal session duration.

## Actual behavior
The user is logged out after about 5 minutes.

## Notes
- Repo: https://github.com/acme-labs/auth-service
- Slack: #eng (C03ENGQ77)

input.title: Migrate docs site off the old static generator
input.description:
## Summary
The docs site (acme-labs/docs-site) currently runs on the old static generator. Track the work to migrate it to the new generator.

## Scope
- Inventory existing pages, templates, plugins, and build config in acme-labs/docs-site
- Choose and set up the replacement generator
- Port content and templates, preserving URLs (add redirects where paths change)
- Verify navigation, search, and internal links on the new build
- Update CI/CD and deployment to publish from the new generator
- Cut over DNS/hosting and decommission the old generator

## Related
- Roadmap: Notion "Docs Roadmap" (9e7a3c15-4d82-4b60-a1f3-6c0d8e2b5f94)
- Repo: https://github.com/acme-labs/docs-site

## Acceptance criteria
- All pages render on the new generator with no broken internal links
- Existing URLs resolve (directly or via redirect)
- Deploy pipeline publishes from the new generator
- Old generator removed from the repo and pipeline

- Any inactivity or idle timeout settings

- Reported as a user-facing bug affecting login sessions.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out of their session approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
A user who logs in should remain logged in for the configured session lifetime (or until they explicitly log out / the session expires per policy).

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out roughly 5 minutes after login.

## Suspected area
Session/token expiry or refresh handling in the login flow of `auth-service` (e.g., session TTL, token lifetime, cookie max-age, or refresh token logic). Not yet investigated.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application as any user.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is required to log in again.

## Impact
Users are interrupted mid-session and must re-authenticate repeatedly.

## Next steps
- Check configured session/token TTL values and any hard-coded 300-second timeouts.
- Verify refresh token behavior and cookie expiry settings.
- Add a regression test asserting sessions persist beyond 5 minutes.

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Users remain logged in for the normal session duration.

## Actual behavior
Sessions end about 5 minutes after login, forcing users to sign in again.

## Relevant code
Login code lives in the GitHub repo `acme-labs/auth-service`. Start investigating session/token expiry and refresh handling there.

## Notes
- Reported in the login flow; affects users generally.
- Possible causes to check: session or token TTL set to 5 minutes, missing or failing refresh-token flow, cookie max-age/expiry mismatch.

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions should persist for the configured session lifetime (not 5 minutes) unless the user logs out or the session expires by design.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out after about 5 minutes.

## Likely location
Login/session code in the `acme-labs/auth-service` repository. Check session/token expiry and refresh logic, and any cookie max-age settings.

## Next steps
- Reproduce and confirm the timeout value
- Identify where the 5-minute expiry is set (session TTL, JWT expiry, or cookie settings)
- Verify whether refresh tokens are being issued and used correctly

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Users remain logged in for the configured session duration.

## Actual behavior
Sessions end about 5 minutes after login, forcing users to sign in again.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is logged out.

## Notes
- Check session/token expiry configuration (e.g., access token TTL, cookie max-age, refresh token handling) for a 5-minute value.
- Check whether refresh logic is running and succeeding.

input.title: Users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
**Bug:** Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

**Affected component:** Login / session handling in `acme-labs/auth-service`

**Expected:** A user who logs in stays logged in for the normal session duration.

**Actual:** The session ends about 5 minutes after login, and the user is logged out.

**Next steps:**
- Check session/token expiry settings (access and refresh token TTLs, cookie max-age) in auth-service.
- Check whether refresh is failing or not being triggered.
- Reproduce locally and confirm the expiry value that causes the logout.

The docs site currently runs on the old static generator. Track the work to migrate it to the new generator.

- [ ] Cut over to the new site and monitor
- [ ] Decommission the old generator setup

- The docs site builds and deploys from the new generator
- Key pages and redirects verified after cutover
- Old generator config removed from the repo

Users remain logged in for the configured session duration.

- Check session/token expiry settings (e.g., access token TTL, refresh token handling, cookie `Max-Age`/`expires`) for a 5-minute value.
- Verify whether refresh logic is running and succeeding.

- Check the session/token expiry configuration in `auth-service` (look for a 5-minute TTL or cookie max-age).
- Verify whether refresh tokens are being issued and used correctly.
- Reproduce with a test account and confirm the timing.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Users remain logged in for the configured session duration.

## Actual behavior
Sessions end after about 5 minutes, forcing users to log in again.

## Suspected area
Login/session code in the `acme-labs/auth-service` repository (session expiry / token TTL / refresh handling).

## Next steps
- Reproduce and confirm the session/token lifetime being applied
- Check session cookie and token expiry settings, and whether refresh is occurring
- Verify fix across affected clients

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out of their session approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
A user who logs in should remain authenticated for the configured session lifetime, without being logged out early.

## Actual behavior
Sessions end about 5 minutes after login, forcing users to sign in again.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is logged out.

## Notes
- Suspect a session/token expiry or refresh issue in auth-service (check session TTL, token lifetime, and refresh-token handling).
- Confirm whether the 5-minute timeout is coming from the access token, the session store, or a cookie max-age setting.

- Choose the target generator and document the decision

- Update the CI/CD build and deploy pipeline
- Cut over DNS/hosting and retire the old generator

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Bug

Users are logged out after approximately 5 minutes of being logged in.

## Expected behavior

Sessions should remain valid for the configured session lifetime, and users should not be logged out after 5 minutes.

## Actual behavior

Users are logged out roughly 5 minutes after logging in.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session has been terminated and the user is required to log in again.

## Notes

- Suspect session/token expiry or cookie lifetime configuration in the auth-service login flow. Worth checking the session TTL, token expiry (e.g. access/refresh token lifetimes), and cookie `Max-Age`/`Expires` settings.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Bug report

**Summary:** Users are logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

**Expected behavior:** The user session remains valid for the configured session lifetime (not 5 minutes) and the user stays logged in while active.

**Actual behavior:** Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

**Area:** Login / session handling in auth-service.

**Suggested investigation:**
- Check session/token expiry settings (e.g., access token TTL, session cookie `Max-Age`/`expires`, refresh token handling) for a 5-minute value.
- Verify whether a refresh flow exists and is being triggered correctly.
- Check for any cache or store TTL (e.g., Redis/session store) set to 300 seconds.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Log in with a valid account.
2. Remain active in the application.
3. Observe the user is logged out after about 5 minutes.

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
A user's session should remain valid for the configured session lifetime, not expire after about 5 minutes.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out roughly 5 minutes after a successful login.

## Notes
- Likely cause to investigate: session/token expiry or refresh configuration in the login code (e.g., access token TTL, cookie max-age, or session store TTL set to 5 minutes).
- Check whether the refresh flow is failing silently after the first token expires.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Remain active (or idle) for about 5 minutes.
3. Observe that the user is logged out.

- [ ] Cut over DNS/hosting and decommission the old generator setup

The docs site is built and deployed from the new generator, old URLs redirect correctly, and the old generator setup is removed.

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Suspected area
Login code lives in the `acme-labs/auth-service` GitHub repository. Start investigation there (session/token expiry and refresh handling).

## Expected behavior
Sessions should persist for the configured session lifetime, with token refresh working as designed.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after login.

## Next steps
- Reproduce and confirm the session/token lifetime in auth-service
- Check token refresh and cookie expiry settings
- Identify whether the change is recent (check auth-service commit history)

input.title: Users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out of their sessions approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions should persist for the configured session lifetime, and users should stay logged in until their session expires or they log out.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is required to log in again.

## Notes
- Check the session/token TTL and expiry configuration in auth-service.
- Check whether refresh token rotation or session renewal is failing or missing.

- Cookie max-age / expiry settings

2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is logged out.

## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions should persist for the configured session duration and not expire after about 5 minutes.

Users are logged out roughly 5 minutes after login.

## Relevant code
Login code lives in the GitHub repo **acme-labs/auth-service**. Check session/token expiry and refresh handling first.

## Next steps
- Reproduce and confirm the exact expiry window
- Check session/token TTL config and refresh-token logic in auth-service
- Verify whether this is tied to a specific client (web/mobile) or all clients

Reported in #eng (C03ENGQ77).

input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Users remain logged in for the normal session duration.

## Actual behavior
Sessions end about 5 minutes after login, forcing users to sign in again.

## Relevant code
Login code lives in the `acme-labs/auth-service` GitHub repository.

## Notes
- Likely related to session/token expiry or refresh handling in auth-service. Not yet investigated.
- Reported via #eng (C03ENGQ77).

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Bug report

**Summary:** Users are logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

**Expected behavior:** The user session should remain valid for the configured session lifetime (or until the user logs out / the session genuinely expires).

**Actual behavior:** Users are logged out about 5 minutes after signing in, regardless of activity.

**Area:** Login / session handling in `auth-service`.

**Suggested investigation:**
- Check session/token expiry settings (e.g., access token TTL, cookie `Max-Age`/expiry, session store TTL) for a 5-minute value.
- Check whether refresh token flow is missing or failing after the first token expires.
- Review recent changes to session or token configuration.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Log in to the application.
2. Remain active (or idle) for about 5 minutes.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is logged out.

- Likely related to session or token lifetime configuration in auth-service. Worth checking session TTL, token expiry, and refresh logic.
- Reported as a login issue affecting users.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Remain active (or idle) for about 5 minutes.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is logged out.

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Problem

Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior

Sessions should remain valid for the configured session lifetime, not expire after about 5 minutes.

## Notes

- Investigate session/token expiry settings (cookie max-age, JWT `exp`, refresh token handling, session store TTL).
- Check whether a 5-minute value is hardcoded or misconfigured in the auth-service login flow.
- Reproduce by logging in and waiting ~5 minutes, then making an authenticated request.

Login / session handling in the `auth-service` repo (acme-labs GitHub org).

- Investigate session/token expiry configuration and refresh logic in auth-service.
- Confirm whether the cause is server-side (token TTL, cookie max-age) or client-side.
- Add a regression test for session duration.

1. Log in to the application.
2. Stay active or idle for about 5 minutes.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is logged out.

**Notes:** Reported from team notes. Further details (environment, affected users, logs) to be added.

- Review recent changes to session or token handling.

Users remain logged in for the normal session duration.

1. Log in to the application.

3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is logged out.

## Notes
- Likely related to session/token expiry or refresh handling in auth-service. Needs investigation to confirm.
- Affected user scope and environments not yet confirmed.

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out of the application approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions remain active for the configured session duration.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out after about 5 minutes.

## Relevant code
Login code lives in the GitHub repo `acme-labs/auth-service`. Start with session/token expiry and refresh handling there.

## Next steps
- Reproduce and confirm the session/token lifetime in use
- Check whether token refresh is failing or not being triggered
- Verify the fix does not break logout or session security

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Bug

Users are being logged out after about 5 minutes of activity.

## Affected code

Login code lives in the GitHub repo `acme-labs/auth-service`.

## Expected behavior

Users stay logged in for the normal session duration.

## Actual behavior

Sessions end after roughly 5 minutes, and users have to log in again.

## Next steps

- Check session/token expiry and refresh settings in `auth-service`.
- Confirm whether the cause is a config value, token TTL, or cookie lifetime.
- Reproduce and add a regression test.

input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Affected component
Login/session code in the GitHub repo `acme-labs/auth-service`.

## Suspected area
Session or token expiry handling. A 5-minute lifetime may come from a misconfigured session TTL, access token expiry, or refresh logic not running.

## Next steps
- Reproduce the logout and confirm the 5-minute timing.
- Check session/token TTL configuration in `auth-service`.
- Verify whether refresh tokens are issued and used correctly.
- Add a test covering session persistence beyond 5 minutes.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Bug

Users are logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior

Users remain logged in for the normal session duration.

## Actual behavior

Sessions end after about 5 minutes, and users are logged out.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is logged out.

## Notes

- Suspect session/token expiry or refresh handling in auth-service.
- Reported in #eng (Slack channel C03ENGQ77).

input.title: Login: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Bug report

Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

**Expected:** Sessions remain active for the configured session lifetime.
**Actual:** Users are logged out after about 5 minutes.

**Likely location:** Login/session code in the `acme-labs/auth-service` repository (session expiry, token TTL, or cookie max-age settings).

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Log in to the app.
2. Stay active or idle for ~5 minutes.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is redirected to login.

**Next steps:** Check session/token expiry configuration in auth-service and confirm whether the 5-minute window comes from a token TTL, cookie max-age, or an idle-timeout setting.

Login / session code in the `acme-labs/auth-service` repository.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions should persist for the configured session lifetime (not 5 minutes) unless the user logs out or the session genuinely expires.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after login.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is logged out.

## Notes for investigation
- Check session/token TTL configuration (access token, refresh token, and session cookie expiry).
- Verify whether refresh token rotation or silent refresh is failing after the first token expires.
- Check whether cookie `Max-Age`/`Expires` or server-side session store TTL is set to 300 seconds.

Users must repeatedly sign in, interrupting their sessions.

3. Observe that the session ends and the user is returned to the login screen.

## Expected
Session remains valid for the configured session duration, or refreshes correctly while the user is active.

## Actual
User is logged out after roughly 5 minutes.

## Repo
https://github.com/acme-labs/auth-service

## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

Sessions should persist for the configured session lifetime and not expire after about 5 minutes.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out roughly 5 minutes after login.

## Suspected area
Login and session code lives in the `acme-labs/auth-service` repository. Start by checking session/token expiry and refresh configuration there.

## Next steps
- Reproduce the logout and confirm the timing.
- Check session/token TTL and refresh logic in `auth-service`.
- Verify the fix does not break existing session handling.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out of their sessions approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Users remain logged in for the configured session duration.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is returned to the login screen.

## Notes
- Likely areas to check: session/token expiry configuration (access vs. refresh token TTL), cookie max-age, and session store TTL in auth-service.

## Summary

The docs site (GitHub: `acme-labs/docs-site`) currently runs on the old static generator. Track the work to migrate it to the new setup.

- Inventory the current pages, templates, plugins, and build steps on the old generator
- Choose and set up the replacement generator/build pipeline
- Port content, templates, and navigation/URL structure, keeping existing URLs working (redirects where paths change)
- Verify the build output matches or improves on the current site (links, search, assets, metadata)
- Update CI/CD and hosting/deploy configuration for the new build
- Cut over to the new site and monitor for regressions
- Decommission the old generator and remove its config and dependencies

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Affected component
Login/session code in the `acme-labs/auth-service` repository.

## Expected behavior
Users remain logged in for the configured session duration.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

## Next steps
- Reproduce the issue and confirm the session/token lifetime in effect.
- Check token expiry, refresh logic, and cookie max-age/expiry settings in `auth-service`.
- Verify whether the 5-minute timeout comes from config or code.

input.body:
## Bug

Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior

Users remain logged in for the configured session duration.

## Actual behavior

Sessions end about 5 minutes after login, forcing users to sign in again.

## Notes

- Check session/token expiry configuration in the auth-service (session TTL, JWT `exp`, cookie `Max-Age`/`expires`).
- Check whether refresh token rotation is failing or not being applied.
- Confirm whether the issue affects all users or only specific clients/platforms.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions remain active for the configured session duration, and users stay logged in until they log out or the session legitimately expires.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

## Suspected area
Login code lives in the `acme-labs/auth-service` GitHub repository. Start investigating session/token expiry and refresh logic there.

## Next steps
- Reproduce the logout after ~5 minutes
- Check session and token TTL configuration and refresh behavior in auth-service
- Confirm whether the issue affects all clients or only specific platforms

Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

- Check whether a short token TTL or cookie max-age is set to 5 minutes, and whether refresh is failing silently.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
A user's session should remain active for the configured session lifetime (not 5 minutes) unless the user logs out or the session expires under the intended policy.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is returned to the login screen.

## Notes
- Likely related to session/token expiry or refresh handling in auth-service. Worth checking the configured session TTL, access token lifetime, and refresh logic.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions remain valid for the configured session lifetime (not a fixed 5 minutes) unless the user logs out or the session expires by design.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after login.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Remain active for about 5 minutes.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is logged out.

## Notes
- Check session/token TTL settings and refresh-token handling in auth-service.
- Verify whether a cookie max-age or JWT `exp` claim is set to 300 seconds.

- Choose and document the target generator
- Port content, templates, and navigation/config to the new generator

- Docs site builds and deploys from the new generator
- No broken internal links; old URLs redirect correctly
- Old generator config and dependencies removed

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Users remain logged in for the configured session lifetime.

## Actual behavior
Sessions end about 5 minutes after login, forcing users to sign in again.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is logged out.

## Notes
- Check session/token expiry configuration (e.g., cookie max-age, JWT `exp`, refresh token handling) in auth-service.
- Verify whether the 5-minute timeout is coming from the auth service or a downstream component.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions remain valid for the configured session lifetime, and users stay logged in until they log out or the session legitimately expires.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in, regardless of activity.

## Notes
- Likely area: session/token expiry or refresh logic in the login code of this service (check session TTL, token lifetime, and refresh handling).
- Please confirm whether the 5-minute window comes from configuration or from a hard-coded value.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out.
3. Observe that the session is terminated and the user is required to log in again.

input.title: Login bug: users are logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions should remain valid for the configured session lifetime, and users should stay logged in until their session expires or they sign out.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without signing out.
3. Observe that the user is logged out.

## Notes
- Likely related to session or token expiry configuration in the login/session code. Worth checking session TTL, token lifetime (e.g. access/refresh token expiry), and cookie `Max-Age`/`Expires` settings.
- Reported from #eng (Slack channel C03ENGQ77).

input.description:
## Summary

The docs site (GitHub: `acme-labs/docs-site`) currently runs on the old static generator. Track the work to migrate it to the new generator.

## Context

- Repo: `acme-labs/docs-site`
- Planning reference: Notion page "Docs Roadmap" (9e7a3c15-4d82-4b60-a1f3-6c0d8e2b5f94)

## Scope / tasks

- [ ] Choose target generator and confirm migration approach
- [ ] Inventory existing pages, templates, plugins, and build config on the old generator
- [ ] Port content and templates to the new generator
- [ ] Verify URLs, redirects, and internal links match the old site
- [ ] Verify search, navigation, and assets work in the new build
- [ ] Update CI/CD build and deploy pipelines
- [ ] Stage review and sign-off
- [ ] Cut over production traffic and decommission the old generator

## Acceptance criteria

- All existing docs pages render on the new generator with no broken links
- Redirects are in place for any changed URLs
- CI/CD deploys the new build; old generator build removed

Login code lives in the `acme-labs/auth-service` GitHub repository.

Users remain logged in for the configured session duration.

Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

- Confirm whether the 5-minute timeout comes from the auth service, a token TTL, or a cookie setting.
- Add a regression test covering session persistence beyond 5 minutes.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.description:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Sessions should persist for the configured session duration without unexpected logouts.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after signing in.

## Likely area
Login/session code in the `auth-service` repo (GitHub org: `acme-labs`). Check session/token expiry and refresh configuration.

## Next steps
- Reproduce and confirm the session lifetime being issued
- Check token/session expiry and refresh logic in `auth-service`
- Verify whether the 5-minute timeout comes from config, cookie settings, or token TTL

- Check token refresh handling and cookie/session TTL configuration.
- Add a regression test covering session duration after login.

input.body:
## Summary
Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior
Users remain logged in for the configured session duration.

## Actual behavior
Users are logged out about 5 minutes after logging in.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Log in to the application.
2. Wait about 5 minutes without logging out manually.
3. Observe that the session has ended and the user is logged out.

## Notes
- Check session/token expiry configuration (e.g., access token TTL, session cookie max-age, refresh token handling) in auth-service.
- Verify whether a refresh flow is running and failing silently after 5 minutes.

input.title: Login bug: users get logged out after 5 minutes
input.body:
## Bug report

Users are being logged out approximately 5 minutes after logging in.

## Expected behavior

Sessions should persist for the configured session lifetime rather than expiring after about 5 minutes.

## Actual behavior

Users are logged out roughly 5 minutes after signing in.

## Notes

- Repository owns the login code, so the likely cause is session/token expiry or refresh logic in auth-service.
- Suggested starting points: session TTL configuration, access/refresh token lifetimes, and any refresh flow that fails silently.
